Founded in 1955, the club competes in the [[Saudi Pro League]], the [[Saudi football league system|top tier of football]] in [[Saudi Arabia]], and is one of three teams never [[List of unrelegated association football clubs#Never relegated|relegated]] from the top flight.{{cite web |title=23 things you need to know about Al-Nassr, the new club of Cristiano Ronaldo|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/articles/article-greater-than-23-things-you-need-to-know-about-al-nassr-the-new-club |website=FIFA |date=4 January 2023 |access-date=3 June 2026}} ==History== {{More citations needed section|date=July 2026}} ===Beginnings and triumphs (1955–1989)=== Al Nassr was established in 1955 by the Al-Ja'ba brothers.Middle East Eye. "Al Nassr: The past and present of Ronaldo's new Saudi team." January 3, 2023. https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/saudi-arabia-nassr-cristiano-ronaldo-new-team-past-present Training took place in an old playground at Gashlat Al-Shortah, west shirts. In addition to the Al-Ja'ba brothers, Ali and Al-Owais, Prince [[Abdul Rahman bin Saud Al Saud]] became the head of Al Nassr, he spent more than 39 years as the president for 3 stints until his death. His love of the team made him accept the challenge of being the president of a second-division club and turning it into a champion, and therefore, he is known as Al-Nassr's Godfather.Arab News. "Prince Abdulrahman bin Saud: The godfather of Al-Nassr." https://www.arabnews.com They were promoted to the first division in 1963. During the 1970s and 1980s, the club won one [[1974–75 Saudi Categorization League|Categorization League]]RSSSF. "Saudi Arabia 1974/75." https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sau75.html and three [[Saudi Pro League|Saudi Premier League]] titles, Five [[King's Cup (Saudi Arabia)|King's Cup]]s, two [[Saudi Crown Prince Cup|Crown Prince's Cup]]s, and one [[Saudi Federation Cup|Federation Cup]]. The team's success was built around the "Saudi Golden Trio" of [[Majed Abdullah]], [[Fahd Al-Herafy|Fahd Al-Bishi]] and [[Mohaisen Al-Jam'an]].{{cite web |url=https://www.al-jazirah.com/1999/19991204/sp12.htm |title=تأسيس النصر |publisher=Al Jazirah |access-date=2025-01-09}} [[File:Al-Nassr Club 1974.jpg|thumb|Picture for the team with trophies won in 1974]] [[File:Majed Abdullah in 1984.jpg|right|175px|thumb|[[Majed Abdullah|Majed Ahmed Abdullah]] is Al Nassr's all-time leader in goals scored and appearances.]] ===End of the Majed Abdullah era (1989–2000)=== In the 1990s (year), Al Nassr managed to win two further [[Saudi Premier League]] titles in the 1993–1994 and 1994–1995 seasons, the 1990 King's Cup and the 1997–1998 Federation Cup.RSSSF. "Saudi Arabia - List of Champions." https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sauchamp.html Towards the end of [[Majed Abdullah]]'s career, he still wasn't able to lift the ultimate prize in [[Union of Arab Football Associations|UAFA]] region; the [[Arab Club Champions Cup]] while the other top clubs in Saudi already succeeded in doing this.Arab News. "Majed Abdullah: Legendary Saudi striker who defined an era." https://www.arabnews.com Despite that, Al Nassr managed to triumph in the continental tournaments.Asian Football Confederation (AFC). Majed Abdullah announced his retirement on 12 April 1998 following Al-Nassr's win in the 1998 Asian Cup Winner's Cup against [[Suwon Samsung Bluewings]] from [[South Korea]] in front of {{gaps|70,000}} fans in Riyadh.Asian Football Confederation (AFC). "1997–98 Asian Cup Winners' Cup Final." https://www.the-afc.com Majed retired at 39 years old as the all-time top scorer of the Saudi League with 189 goals and is also Al-Nassr's all-time top scorer with 260 goals, a record that was considered untouchable until the coming of [[Abderrazak Hamdallah]].Saudi Pro League. "All-time Top Scorers and Records." https://www.spl.com.sa After becoming champion of the [[Asian Super Cup]], Al-Nassr was eligible to represent the [[Asian Football Confederation|AFC]] region in the first [[2000 FIFA Club World Championship|FIFA Club World Cup]]. In that championship Al-Nassr played against [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Raja Casablanca]] and finished 3rd in the group, the club became the first team to officially represent Asia in an international tournament, which was held in Brazil from 5 January to 14 January, in the year 2000. The nickname "''The Global One (Al-Alami)''" was obtained following their respective participation in the Club World Cup. Following the retirement of the Golden Trio, Al-Nassr’s squad reached the [[FIFA Club World Cup]] for the first time. The club signed international players including Ivory Coast forward [[Fadel Keïta]] and former [[Barcelona]] midfielder [[Julio César Baldivieso]].{{Cite web |title=Fadel Keita |url=https://www.national-football-teams.com/player/30002/Fadel_Keita.html |website=National Football Teams |access-date=2026-07-25}} Results declined in subsequent seasons. In 2006–07 Al-Nassr finished ninth with 21 points and avoided relegation on the final matchday. Honorary members, including [[Majed Abdullah]], intervened to begin a long-term restructuring of the club’s management. During this period Al-Hilal recorded more derby victories against Al-Nassr than in any previous era.{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Saudi Arabia 2006/07 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sau07.html |website=RSSSF |date=2020-09-02 |access-date=2026-07-25}} ===Revival (2008–2015)=== [[File:Al-Nasr crowd.jpg|thumb|Al-Nassr supporters at the [[King Fahd International Stadium]] in 2008]] After a major overhaul of the playing staff, Al-Nassr defeated city rivals [[Al-Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] to win the 2008 Federation Cup. In 2009 the club signed [[Mohammad Al-Sahlawi]] from [[Al-Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]] for a reported SR32 million, then a domestic record.{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} In his first season Al-Sahlawi scored 21 goals in 36 matches and was named Young Player of the Year by STC. Al-Nassr finished third in the 2009–10 league and qualified for the [[2011 AFC Champions League]].{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Saudi Arabia 2009/10 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sau2010.html |website=RSSSF |date=2014-04-10 |access-date=2026-07-25}} ====2011 AFC Champions League==== Al-Nassr finished second in their group. Results included a 2–2 draw with [[Pakhtakor FC|Pakhtakor]] (goal by loaned player [[Bader Al-Mutawa]]), a 2–1 win over [[Esteghlal F.C.|Esteghlal]] ([[Hussein Abdulghani]]), a 1–0 defeat to [[Al Sadd SC|Al-Sadd]], a further draw with Al-Sadd, a 4–0 victory over Pakhtakor (goals by [[Saud Hamood]], Al-Sahlawi and two by Al-Mutawa), and a 2–1 loss to Esteghlal. In the round of 16 the club was eliminated 4–1 by [[Zob Ahan Esfahan F.C.|Zob Ahan]]. Al-Mutawa scored five goals in the competition before returning to Kuwait.{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Asian Club Competitions 2011 |url=https://www.rsssf.com/tablesa/ascup2011.html |website=RSSSF |date=2016-03-17 |access-date=2026-07-25}} ====League and cup success==== Under coach [[Francisco Maturana]] in 2011–12 Al-Nassr reached the Crown Prince Cup final but lost to Al-Hilal on penalties.{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} In 2013–14, with [[José Daniel Carreño]] as coach, the team recorded a 22-match unbeaten run and won both the [[Saudi Pro League]] and the Crown Prince Cup against Al-Hilal, qualifying for the 2015 AFC Champions League.{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Saudi Arabia 2013/14 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sau2014.html |website=RSSSF |date=2017-08-31 |access-date=2026-07-25}} Al-Nassr retained the league title in 2014–15. The side lost the King’s Cup final and exited the Crown Prince Cup in the semi-finals. In the 2015 AFC Champions League the team finished bottom of a group containing [[FC Bunyodkor|Bunyodkor]], [[Al-Duhail SC|Al-Duhail]] and [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]]. Al-Sahlawi scored 25 goals in 37 appearances that season. René Higuita was appointed coach but the club again failed to progress beyond the group stage of the 2016 AFC Champions League.{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Asian Club Competitions 2015 |url=https://www.rsssf.com/tablesa/ascup2015.html |website=RSSSF |date=2018-11-22 |access-date=2026-07-25}}{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Asian Club Competitions 2016 |url=https://www.rsssf.com/tablesa/ascup2016.html |website=RSSSF |date=2019-03-07 |access-date=2026-07-25}} ===Hamdallah era (2016–2022)=== Al-Nassr finished third in the 2016–17 league behind [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]] and Al-Hilal. The club were runners-up in both the Crown Prince Cup and the King’s Cup and did not qualify for the AFC Champions League in 2017 or 2018. Al-Sahlawi scored 10, 11 and 12 league goals across the three seasons from 2015–16 to 2017–18.{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Saudi Arabia 2016/17 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sau2017.html |website=RSSSF |date=2020-09-02 |access-date=2026-07-25}} In March 2018 coach [[Gustavo Quinteros]] signed [[Sultan Al-Ghannam]] on a free transfer from [[Al-Faisaly FC|Al-Faisaly]]. In the summer the club added Moroccan players [[Abderrazak Hamdallah]] and [[Nordin Amrabat]].{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} Hamdallah finished the 2018–19 season as league top scorer with 34 goals and helped Al-Nassr win the title. He also scored heavily in the King’s Cup, including multiple hat-tricks. At the end of the calendar year he was recognised by the IFFHS as the world’s leading goalscorer with 57 goals. Al-Sahlawi left for [[Al-Shabab FC (Riyadh)|Al-Shabab]].{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Saudi Arabia 2018/19 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/sau2019.html |website=RSSSF |date=2020-12-02 |access-date=2026-07-25}} Al-Nassr won the Saudi Super Cup in January 2020 (1–1 draw with Al-Taawoun, Hamdallah scoring) and again in January 2021 (3–0 against Al-Hilal).{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} In the 2019 AFC Champions League the club reached the quarter-finals before losing to Al-Sadd; Hamdallah scored four goals. In the 2020 edition Al-Nassr reached the semi-finals, losing on penalties to Persepolis. Hamdallah shared the golden boot with seven goals.{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Asian Club Competitions 2019 |url=https://www.rsssf.com/tablesa/ascup2019.html |website=RSSSF |date=2020-12-16 |access-date=2026-07-25}}{{Cite web |last=Stokkermans |first=Karel |title=Asian Club Competitions 2020 |url=https://www.rsssf.com/tablesa/ascup2020.html |website=RSSSF |date=2022-03-24 |access-date=2026-07-25}} Hamdallah’s contract was terminated in November 2020 although he remained available until the end of the season. In May and June 2021 the club signed [[Talisca]] (reported €9.5 million) and [[Vincent Aboubakar]] (reported €6 million). Both scored on debut in a 4–1 win over Damac in August 2021. Under coaches [[Miguel Ángel Russo]] and later [[Rudi Garcia]] the team finished without major trophies in 2021–22. Talisca scored a hat-trick in a 4–1 win at Al-Raed.{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} ===Ronaldo era (2023–present)=== [[File:(Tehran) Persepolis F.C. v Al Nassr FC, 19 September 2023 14 (cropped).jpg|thumb|[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] captaining Al-Nassr in 2023]] On 30 December 2022 Al-Nassr signed [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] on a two-and-a-half-year contract later extended. The reported annual salary was among the highest ever paid to a footballer.{{Cite news |title=Cristiano Ronaldo completes deal to join Saudi Arabian club Al Nassr |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/dec/30/cristiano-ronaldo-al-nassr-saudi-arabia |work=The Guardian |date=2022-12-30 |access-date=2026-07-25}}{{Cite news |title=Ronaldo joins Saudi Arabian club Al Nassr until 2025 |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/ronaldo-joins-saudi-arabian-club-al-nassr-saudi-state-tv-2022-12-30/ |work=Reuters |date=2022-12-30 |access-date=2026-07-25}} Al-Nassr finished second in the 2022–23 Saudi Pro League. ==== 2023–2024 ==== Al-Nassr won the 2023 Arab Club Champions Cup. After drawing 0–0 with Al-Shabab, beating US Monastir 4–1 (Ronaldo scoring) and drawing 1–1 with Zamalek, the side defeated Raja Casablanca 3–1 and Al-Shorta 1–0 (Ronaldo penalty). In the final against Al-Hilal, Al-Nassr came from 1–0 down, finished with ten men, and won 2–1 after extra time with both goals scored by Ronaldo. He finished as the tournament’s top scorer with six goals.{{Cite news |title=10-man Al-Nassr win Arab Club Champions Cup thanks to Cristiano Ronaldo double |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/aug/12/10-man-al-nassr-win-arab-club-champions-cup-thanks-to-cristiano-ronaldo-double |work=The Guardian |date=2023-08-12 |access-date=2026-07-25}} In the summer of 2023 the club added [[Otávio (footballer, born 1995)|Otávio]], [[Sadio Mané]], [[Aymeric Laporte]], [[Seko Fofana]], [[Marcelo Brozović]], [[Aziz Behich]] and [[Alex Telles]].{{Cite news |title=Aymeric Laporte: Manchester City accept undisclosed offer from Al-Nassr for Spain defender |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66519408 |work=BBC Sport |date=2023-08-16 |access-date=2026-07-25}}{{Cite news |title=Sadio Mane leaves Bayern Munich and joins Cristiano Ronaldo at Saudi side Al Nassr |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4729257/2023/08/01/sadio-mane-saudi-transfer-al-nassr-bayern/ |work=The Athletic |date=2023-08-01 |access-date=2026-07-25}} At the end of 2023 Al-Nassr stood second in the league. The side topped their AFC Champions League group unbeaten and reached the King’s Cup semi-finals. Talisca led the AFC Champions League scoring charts with eight group-stage goals.{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} Ronaldo was named the IFFHS world’s best goalscorer for 2023 with 54 goals.{{Cite web |date=2024-01-01 |title=IFFHS MEN'S WORLD BEST GOAL SCORER 2023 |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-mens-world-best-goal-scorer-2023-3288 |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=iffhs.com |language=en}} Al-Nassr were eliminated from the 2023–24 AFC Champions League by Al-Ain on penalties after a 4–4 aggregate. The club also lost the King’s Cup final on penalties, exited the Super Cup in the semi-finals, and finished second in the league with a club-record 82 points. Ronaldo won the golden boot and set a new single-season league scoring record.{{Cite web |title=Cristiano Ronaldo sets Saudi Pro League single-season scoring record |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/ronaldo-sets-saudi-pro-league-season-scoring-record-while-alhilal-finishes-unbeaten |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=www.foxsports.com |language=en-US}} ==== 2024–2025 ==== President Ibrahim al-Muhaidib resigned in 2024. New signings included [[Mohamed Simakan]], [[Ângelo Gabriel]], [[Wesley (footballer, born 2005)|Wesley]] and [[Bento (footballer)|Bento]]. [[Luís Castro (footballer, born 1961)|Luís Castro]] was replaced by [[Stefano Pioli]] in September 2024. The club launched “Nassr TV” in partnership with DAZN.{{citation needed|date=July 2026}} In January 2025 Majid Al-Jam’an replaced Guido Fienga as executive director. The club signed [[Jhon Durán]] and sold Seko Fofana to Rennes for a reported €20 million. In July 2025, José Semedo became acting CEO, Simão Coutinho was appointed sporting director, and [[Jorge Jesus]] replaced Pioli as manager. Further arrivals included [[João Félix]], [[Iñigo Martínez]] and [[Kingsley Coman]]. Later in August 2025, Al-Nassr lost the Saudi Super Cup final to Al-Ahli on penalties.{{Cite web |last=League |first=Saudi Pro |date=2025-08-23 |title=Al Ahli defeat Al Nassr on penalties to seal Saudi Super Cup |url=https://www.spl.com.sa/news/al-ahli-defeat-al-nassr-on-penalties-to-seal-saudi-super-cup |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Saudi Pro League |language=en}} ====2025–2026==== During the 2025–26 season under Jesus, Al-Nassr reached the AFC Champions League 2 Final but were defeated by Gamba Osaka. The club went on to win the Saudi Pro League title. Following the season, [[Jorge Jesus]] departed the club. [[Ange Postecoglou|Ange Postecoglu]] was subsequently appointed as manager, with [[Samú Costa|Samu Costa]] joining the squad as a new signing. ==Crests and colours== ===Crests=== File:Al Nassr 1955.png|1955 File:Al Nassr 1971.png|1971 File:Al Nassr 2009.png|2009 File:Al Nassr 2011.png|2011 File:Al Nassr FC Logo.svg|2020 File:Nassr FC Logo.svg|2025 Al-Nassr ([[Arabic]]: النصر‎) is the Arabic word for "victory".
